title: Can LLM Agents Select and Engage with Biological Tools? An Initial Biosecurity Assessment (rand, 2026-06-25)
abstract:
Corpus sentences naming ABC-Bench, plus the cited release-decision sentences (system-card corpus docs.sqlite, document slug in brackets):
[rand-gpt-5-independent-eval-2] 3 Liu et al., “ABC-Bench”; Cai et al., “Agentic BAIM-LLM Evaluation (ABLE).” 4 For more information, see https://cursor.com/cli 5 See Table 2.3 for the list of models. v Key Findings • We find that LLM Agents are capable of performing many initial interactions with BTs, suggesting that they may facilitate BT use by nonexpert actors, and that more targeted testing of LLM Agent design abilities is therefore warranted. • LLMs are highly capable of identifying BTs for specific functions but performed worse when required to map BT functions onto contextualized biological design scenarios.
[rand-gpt-5-independent-eval-2] In Chapter 2, we describe our evaluation and case study design and provide additional details on the threat models, BTs, LLM Agent framework, and implementation process of the 25 Mitchener et al., “BixBench”; Liu et al., “ABC-Bench”; Laurent et al., “LAB-Bench”; Cai et al., “Agentic BAIM-LLM Evaluation (ABLE).” 26 OpenAI, “OpenAI o1 System Card”.
[rand-gpt-5-independent-eval-2] Liu, Andrew Bo, Samira Nedungadi, Bryce Cai, Alex Kleinman, Harmon Bhasin, and Seth Donoughe, “ABC-Bench: An Agentic Bio-Capabilities Benchmark for Biosecurity,” paper presented at the 39th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2025) Workshop: Biosecurity Safeguards for Generative AI, December 6, 2025.
